chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to him, 'A person died while he was in a state of major ritual impurity (junub). How should he be washed, and what portion of the water suffices for him?' He said, 'He is washed with one washing; that suffices for him for his major impurity and for the washing of the deceased, because the two obligations have combined into one sanctity.'

key_terms.جُنُب: One in a state of major ritual impurity (junub)
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: He is washed (ritual bath for deceased)

ai.seo_question: How many times should a deceased person be washed if they died in a state of major impurity?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a single washing suffices for a deceased person who died in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), as the two obligations merge into one. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that when multiple ritual requirements coincide on a single entity, they are discharged by a single act unless specified otherwise. The hadith underscores the practical ease in funeral rites while maintaining ritual purity standards.
